q: The net force acting on an object doubles, and at the same time the mass of the object is halved. By what factor does the acceleration change?
a: It becomes four times as great. The acceleration $a = \dfrac{\Sigma F}{m}$ doubles because of the force and doubles once more when the mass is halved: $2\cdot 2 = 4$.

q: An elevator moves upward and slows down as it stops at a floor. Which is greater during the slowing down, the tension in the supporting rope or the weight of the elevator? Justify your answer.
a: The weight is greater. The elevator slows down while moving up, so its acceleration and net force point down: $T - G = ma$, where $a < 0$, so $T < G$.

q: What is one newton? Express it using kilograms, metres and seconds.
a: One newton is the force that gives a mass of $1\,\text{kg}$ an acceleration of $1\,\text{m/s}^2$. So $1\,\text{N} = 1\,\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}^2$.
